st.headline: Wall St rises on the day but falls for the week; bond yields and Iran in focus
st.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 517.80 points, or 0.98 per cent, to 53,277.01.
fullText: NEW YORK - The main US stock indexes closed higher on Aug 21 but showed declines for the week, which was marked by investor jitters over fluctuating government bond yields and a lack of clarity on progress in the Middle East.
The S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq snapped three-week winning streaks, while the Dow registered its second consecutive weekly loss.
Equity investors have been taking their cues from the direction of US government bond yields in recent sessions as the prospect of higher borrowing costs dampened risk appetite.
Stocks had closed lower on Aug 20 as bond yields rose while equities had advanced on Aug 19 as bond yields fell.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Aug 20 that the government could further increase its Treasury repurchases after a surprise announcement on Aug 19 that it would spend double the expected amount on bond buybacks.
After a seesaw trading week on Wall Street, Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer at Northlight Asset Management in Charlotte, North Carolina, said that Aug 21 seemed calmer.
“In the middle of the week, equity investors were concerned yields could be on a one-way trip higher. With the Treasury Department announcement, investors aren’t as worried any more,” he said.

Also helping to ease investor worries was economic data on Aug 21, which showed that the strongest growth in the US services sector in nearly two years powered a sharp acceleration in overall business activity in August.
This offset a slowing of growth in a manufacturing sector that is being restrained by reduced stock building and supply disruptions from the Iran war.
Earlier, UBS Global Wealth Management raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 to 8,100, citing a stronger earnings outlook and robust corporate profit growth.

Adding to inflation concerns, however, oil futures settled higher for a sixth straight day, after US President Donald Trump threatened economic sanctions on Iran’s trading partners, raising expectations of tighter supply.
For the week, Brent futures gained 6.39 per cent while US crude rose 5.66 per cent.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 517.80 points, or 0.98 per cent, to 53,277.01, the S&P 500 gained 33.21 points, or 0.43 per cent, to 7,674.37 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 113.29 points, or 0.44 per cent, to 26,180.46.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell 1.43 per cent, the Nasdaq declined 2.05 per cent, and the Dow fell 0.85 per cent. The Russell 2000 small-cap index fell 1.65 per cent for its biggest drop since the week starting June 1.

Among the S&P 500’s 11 major industry sectors, most advanced on Aug 21. Materials outperformed with a 2.2 per cent advance, followed by a 1.3 per cent advance in healthcare and a 1 per cent gain in financial stocks.

Utilities was the biggest laggard by far, finishing down 2.3 per cent compared with a 0.2 per cent drop for energy , the next-biggest loser. In individual stocks, Ross Stores finished up 4.4 per cent after the value retailer raised its annual profit forecasts and reported better-than-expected quarterly results.

Shares of retail investor platform Robinhood rallied 13.7 per cent. Crypto exchange operator Coinbase Global climbed 8.2 per cent and bitcoin-hoarder Strategy added 6 per cent as bitcoin advanced 6.4 per cent and touched its highest levels since mid-May.
In the week ahead, investor attention will turn to quarterly results from AI chip leader Nvidia and software companies such as Intuit, Salesforce and CrowdStrike .

Next week’s data releases include July’s Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, which is the US Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge. Tame July readings for consumer and producer prices had knocked down bets of an imminent central bank rate hike.
Investors are also waiting for Fed chair Kevin Warsh’s speech at the Jackson Hole symposium at the end of next week.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.68-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange, where there were 214 new highs and 118 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 3,186 stocks rose and 1,725 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.85-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 13 new 52-week highs and four new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 91 new highs and 76 new lows.
On US exchanges, 14.91 billion shares changed hands compared with the 16.62 billion average for the last 20 sessions, according to LSEG data. REUTERS

cna.headline: Starc takes five wickets, Bangladesh 35 for six at lunch in second test
cna.teaser: Starc takes five wickets, Bangladesh 35 for six at lunch in second test
fullText: Aug 22 : Australia paceman Mitchell Starc took five wickets in 22 balls in a brilliant spell of quick bowling as Bangladesh staggered to lunch at 35 for six on day one of the second test in Mackay, Queensland on Saturday.
• Starc's was the sixth-fastest five-wicket haul in tests. The left-hander holds the record for the fastest, having taken five wickets in 15 balls against West Indies in Kingston last year.
• Bangladesh all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz was 11 not out, with number eight Hasan Mahmud on eight at the break.

• Starc removed both Bangladesh openers, captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and wicketkeeper Litton Das for ducks to leave the tourists at 12 for five, after Australia captain Pat Cummins won the toss and elected to field.
• Opener Tanzid Hasan followed in Starc's next over with a loose drive sending a nick to Beau Webster in the slips, before Shanto was trapped lbw on the next ball, leaving Bangladesh at 9 for three.
• Starc grabbed his fourth wicket when number three Mominul Haque drove at a full, wider delivery, nicking to Green at the gully. He took his fifth with another lbw to remove Das.
• Cummins bowled Bangladesh number five Mushfiqur Rahim for five on a bouncy pitch likened to a typical Gabba wicket.
• Bangladesh lead the series 1-0 after a nine-wicket win in the series-opener in Darwin.
• Matt Renshaw to open the batting for Australia in his first test in over three years, with Jake Weatherald dropped after consecutive failures in Darwin.
• Bangladesh made one change to their Darwin XI, bringing in left-arm paceman Shoriful Islam after his recovery from a hamstring injury. He replaced fellow quick Ebadot Hossain.
• Mackay's Great Barrier Reef Arena became Australia's 12th test venue.
A single handpicked story that we think you shouldn't miss. Just one a day.

listening.title: Singapore Braces for Global Trade Winds
listening.transcript: As global tensions rise, Singapore is closely monitoring potential economic disruptions. Economists warn that new tariffs could impact the city-state's export-reliant manufacturing sector, particularly electronics. However, local supply chains remain robust due to ongoing diversification efforts. The government encourages local businesses to look for new opportunities in regional markets like ASEAN.

economistArticle.title: The Cost of Walls: Singapore and the New Tariff Era
paras: With the potential return of aggressive protectionist policies in major economies like the United States, trade barriers are rising once more. The global effective tariff, once on a downward trajectory due to decades of multilateral agreements, is poised for a sharp uptick. This shift poses a severe threat to the smooth flow of goods that has underpinned global prosperity.

As a hyper-connected, trade-dependent city-state, Singapore is uniquely vulnerable to these protectionist shifts. With a trade-to-GDP ratio exceeding 300%, the island nation relies heavily on open global markets. Any escalation in tariffs between the world's largest economies disrupts supply chains that run directly through Southeast Asian shipping lanes and air hubs.

Although tariffs are often framed as a tax on foreign competitors, economic history demonstrates that the ultimate burden falls on domestic consumers and businesses. Intermediate goods—such as microchips, chemical compounds, and machinery parts—are taxed at every border crossing. Consequently, final retail prices inflate, eroding consumer purchasing power and compressing corporate margins.

To bypass these punitive duties, multinational corporations are actively reorganising their footprints. This has accelerated the "China-plus-one" strategy, where businesses set up secondary manufacturing bases in countries like Vietnam, Malaysia, and Indonesia. While this geographic shift provides a buffer, it also introduces operational inefficiencies and increases capital expenditure.

To thrive in this fractured landscape, Singapore must continue to leverage its reputation as a trusted neutral hub. By expanding its network of high-quality free trade agreements and investing heavily in advanced manufacturing and digital services, the city-state can insulate itself from the worst effects of global protectionism. In an era of economic nationalism, agility remains Singapore's ultimate competitive advantage.
economistArticle.cn:
随着美国等主要经济体可能重新推行激进的保护主义政策，贸易壁垒再次抬头。由于数十年的多边协定，全球实际关税曾一度呈下降趋势，如今却蓄势待发。这一转变对支撑全球繁荣的货物顺畅流通构成了严重威胁。

作为一个高度互联、依赖贸易的城市国家，新加坡在这些保护主义转变面前显得尤为脆弱。由于贸易占国内生产总值（GDP）的比例超过300%，这个岛国高度依赖开放的全球市场。世界最大经济体之间关税的任何升级，都会扰乱直接穿过东南亚航道和航空枢纽的供应链。

尽管关税通常被塑造成对外国竞争对手征收的税，但经济历史表明，最终的负担其实落在了国内消费者和企业身上。半成品——如微芯片、化学化合物和机器零件——在每次越过国界时都会被征税。因此，最终零售价格上涨，削弱了消费者的购买力，并压缩了企业的利润空间。

为了绕过这些惩罚性关税，跨国公司正在积极重新调整其业务版图。这加速了“中国加一”战略，即企业在越南、马来西亚和印度尼西亚等国设立二级制造基地。虽然这种地理上的转变提供了缓冲，但也带来了运营效率低下并增加了资本支出。

为了在这个四分五裂的格局中蓬勃发展，新加坡必须继续利用其作为值得信赖的中立枢纽的声誉。通过扩大其高质量自由贸易协定网络，并大力投资先进制造业和数字服务，这个城市国家可以使自己免受全球保护主义的最坏影响。在经济民族主义时代，敏捷性依然是新加坡的核心竞争优势。

gems.s: Although tariffs are often framed as a tax on foreign competitors, economic history demonstrates that the ultimate burden falls on domestic consumers and businesses.
gems.why: This sentence effectively uses contrastive framing ('framed as... economic history demonstrates that...') to debunk a common political myth. This is a powerful rhetorical device for analytical writing. / 这句话通过对比性框架（‘被塑造成……而经济历史表明……’）成功揭示并反驳了一个常见的政治迷思。这在分析性写作中是一种非常强大的修辞手法。

gems.s: In an era of economic nationalism, agility remains Singapore's ultimate competitive advantage.
gems.why: This is a concise, punchy concluding sentence that uses a parallel noun phrase ('In an era of X, Y remains Z') to leave a memorable final impression on the reader. / 这是一个简明扼要、富有冲击力的结语。它运用平行名词短语（‘在X的时代，Y依然是Z’）为读者留下了难以忘怀的最终印象。
